I fixed the bug, and all 6 tests pass (`python3 -m pytest -q`).

**Root cause:** `parse_price` in `inventory.py` turned every comma into a dot whenever the string contained one. `"1,234.50"` became `"1.234.50"`, which `float` rejects.

**Fix:** a comma is now treated as a thousands separator when th
…
or `1,234,567`. That means digit groups of exactly three after each comma, plus either a dot or a second comma group. In every other case the comma is still a decimal comma, so `"12,50"` still gives `12.5`. A lone `"1,234"` has no dot or second group, so it is read as the European decimal `1.234`, as the issue specifies.

**Tests:** I added regression tests for `"1,234.50"`, `"$1,234,567.89"` and `"1,234,567"`. Before the fix, the two new tests failed (they raised `ValueError`). The existing tests for `"12.50"`, `"$3"`, `"12,50"` and `total_value` still pass, and I didn't change `total_value`.
